provenance: Five English private-person scenarios authored inside the Cloak repository. Public-source clauses and layouts are adapted, not copied wholesale. Medical, immigration, and workplace facts are entirely synthetic.
threat_model: Primary: GPT-5.6 sees only the sanitized document and has no auxiliary roster. Stress tier: the same controller receives a synthetic four-person roster. The roster is evaluation-only and is never available to product sessions.

scenarios.task: Review this employment agreement from the employee's perspective. Identify the five most employee-unfavorable clauses, explain the practical risk of each, identify important protections that are missing or one-sided, and give a prioritized list of negotiation questions. Do not claim to provide legal advice.
expected_findings: The automatic renewal and 90-day non-renewal window can trap the employee or require early action.
The non-compete is broad in geography, role, and contemplated lines of business and lasts twelve months.
The arbitration clause is asymmetric because the employer keeps court access for intellectual-property claims.
The signing-bonus clawback applies even when the employee is terminated without cause and lacks a clear cap or waiver.
The invention-assignment language reaches work developed outside working hours and needs a prior-inventions carve-out.
The employee should ask about severance, good-reason resignation, fee shifting, governing law, and a narrower restrictive covenant.
scenarios.boundary_note: The clauses, not the employee's identity, are the substance; this is the expected sweet spot.

scenarios.document:
EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This agreement is entered into on 8 September 2025 between Meridian Clinical Systems LLC, with offices in Raleigh, North Carolina, and Nora Bennett, employee number EMP-44719, residing at 44 Larkspur Way, Raleigh, NC 27603. Notices to the employee may also be sent to nora.bennett@private.example. Ms. Bennett will serve as Director of Product Operations for the employer's clinical workflow business. Her base salary is $146,000 and she will receive a $20,000 signing bonus.

1. Term and renewal. Employment begins 22 September 2025 for an initial two-year term. The agreement renews automatically for one-year periods unless either party gives written notice at least ninety days before the current term ends. The employer may change title, reporting line, and primary work location within North Carolina when it determines there is a business need.

2. Restrictive covenant. During employment and for twelve months after termination, the employee may not work in any capacity for a business offering products or services that compete with any line of business the employer conducted or seriously considered during the prior twenty-four months. The restriction applies in every state or province where the employer had a customer, prospective customer, or documented expansion plan. Passive ownership below two percent of a public company is permitted.

3. Confidentiality and inventions. The employee assigns to the employer all inventions, processes, writings, and improvements that relate to the employer's actual or anticipated business, whether created during or outside working hours. No schedule of the employee's prior inventions is attached. The employee may make legally protected reports to government agencies.

4. Bonus repayment. If employment ends for any reason before the second anniversary, the employee must repay the signing bonus on a prorated basis within thirty days. The clause applies to resignation, termination for cause, termination without cause, disability, and a material reduction in duties.

5. Disputes. Except for claims the employer brings concerning confidential information, inventions, or restrictive covenants, every dispute must proceed through final and binding arbitration before one arbitrator. Each party pays its own legal fees. The employer may seek temporary or permanent injunctive relief in court without first completing arbitration.

6. Termination. The employer may terminate without cause on thirty days' notice and owes only salary earned through the termination date. The agreement contains no severance promise, no good-reason resignation right, and no reimbursement of employee legal fees.

scenarios.task: Prepare a concise, prioritized list of questions this patient should take to the next specialist appointment. Flag medication-safety issues, missing monitoring, interactions between the conditions, and symptoms that may require urgent attention. Distinguish questions from medical conclusions.
expected_findings: The positive latent-TB screen requires clarification and treatment planning before or during biologic immunosuppression.
Pregnancy planning should trigger a coordinated medication and disease-control review rather than abrupt medication cessation.
Persistent right-upper-quadrant pain and elevated liver enzymes need evaluation, especially with isoniazid exposure or planned treatment.
The record should clarify vaccine status and avoid live vaccines during biologic therapy.
The patient should ask about CBC, liver tests, inflammatory markers, infection warning signs, and which specialist coordinates care.
scenarios.boundary_note: The condition, treatment, language role, and pregnancy-planning stack is both medically necessary and potentially identifying within a small community.

scenarios.document:
SPECIALIST HANDOFF SUMMARY

Patient: Leila Haddad. MRN-0081742. Contact: leila.haddad@private.example, +1 313-555-0187. Referring site: Cedar Bridge Community Clinic.

Ms. Haddad is a 34-year-old Arabic medical interpreter in the Detroit area with ileocolonic Crohn's disease diagnosed after hospitalization in 2021. She currently uses adalimumab 40 mg every other week and reports that abdominal cramping returns two to three days before each dose. She has not had a surveillance colonoscopy since early 2022.

An employment-health screen six weeks ago showed positive latent-tuberculosis screening. Chest radiography was reported as negative, but the chart does not contain the radiology report or an infectious-disease plan. Primary care discussed isoniazid but deferred starting it until gastroenterology reviewed the biologic therapy.

Laboratory results from last month show ALT 86 U/L, AST 58 U/L, hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, and mildly elevated C-reactive protein. She describes intermittent right-upper-quadrant discomfort, fatigue, and two episodes of night sweats without measured fever. No hepatitis serologies are visible in the shared record.

The patient is planning pregnancy within the next year and asks whether she should stop adalimumab before conception. She takes an over-the-counter prenatal vitamin and ibuprofen several times per week for joint pain. Vaccination history is incomplete; the record lists an influenza vaccine but no recent pneumococcal, hepatitis B, or shingles documentation.

The requested visit should reconcile infection risk, Crohn's control, liver-test abnormalities, anemia, pregnancy planning, vaccination timing, and which clinician will coordinate follow-up.

scenarios.task: Review this draft immigration declaration for internal consistency and evidentiary gaps. Identify the facts that most strongly support the claim, dates or details that need clarification, corroborating evidence to request, and passages whose generalization would materially weaken the case. Do not decide legal eligibility or provide a legal conclusion.
expected_findings: The chronology around the procurement report, first threat, assault, police response, and relocation must be internally consistent.
The declaration needs the original procurement email, audit records, clinic letter, police receipt, threatening messages, and cousin or supervisor statements where available.
The explanation for delayed departure and the two returns to San Isidro needs detail because an adjudicator may view it as inconsistent with fear.
The link between the attackers and the contractor is asserted but needs corroboration or a clearer basis for the belief.
Internal relocation failed only after a distinctive work-history clue exposed the declarant; removing that detail materially changes the case.
scenarios.boundary_note: The rare chronology and local institutions are the evidence. Generalizing them enough to defeat a roster attacker can materially weaken the requested legal-document review.

scenarios.document:
DRAFT DECLARATION

I, Ana Lucía Quintero, A-number A209-771-483, can be reached at ana.quintero@private.example and +1 617-555-0144. I make this declaration from my own knowledge.

I worked as a payroll analyst for the municipality of San Isidro. In May 2023 I noticed that three workers listed on an irrigation-modernization contract shared bank details with relatives of the contractor's local manager. On 19 May I sent a spreadsheet and written report to the municipal audit office. My supervisor told me not to discuss it outside our department.

On 2 June, a caller who knew my daughter's school route said I should withdraw the report. I kept working because I supported my mother and daughter. I returned twice to San Isidro after short visits to my aunt because the municipality said the audit was still open and I feared losing access to the records. The declaration should explain those returns more clearly.

On 14 August 2023, two men stopped me near the eastern bus depot after work. One referred to the irrigation spreadsheet before they struck my shoulder and ribs. A vendor helped me reach Santa Marta clinic. The clinic letter dated 18 September describes bruising but does not identify the attackers. I reported the assault; the police gave me a receipt but did not take my phone messages or contact the audit office.

In October I moved to Puerto Nieve and used my middle name. I found temporary payroll work at a cooperative. Six weeks later, a stranger asked a coworker whether the woman who had configured San Isidro's unusual three-stage payroll approval system worked there. I left that night. I believe this detail connected me to my former municipal job, although I do not know who supplied it.

I departed the country in January 2024. I still have screenshots of two threats, the clinic letter, the police receipt, and a copy of my audit email, but not the underlying municipal spreadsheet. My former supervisor and cousin witnessed parts of these events but are afraid to provide signed statements. The chronology must preserve the sequence from the procurement report to the threats, the assault, and the internal relocation attempt.

scenarios.task: Review this credit-card statement for the cardholder. Explain the most important fees, interest, utilization, payment risks, and unusual spending patterns; identify any transaction that merits verification; and give a prioritized, numerically grounded action plan for the next billing cycle. expected_findings: The balance is about 89% of the $8,000 credit line, creating high utilization and little remaining credit.
Paying only the $96 minimum while the purchase APR is 24.99% will prolong repayment and increase interest.
The $39 late fee and $74.18 interest charge should be highlighted, with a request for a one-time fee waiver if appropriate.
The two Harbor Ferry Terminal charges on the same day and the out-of-pattern Montreal hotel charge merit verification.
The action plan should prioritize on-time payment, stopping new charges, paying above minimum, and checking autopay and fraud alerts.
scenarios.boundary_note: Amounts and transaction risks matter; the cardholder's identity does not.

scenarios.source_title: EEOC sample charge and non-retaliation notice structure
utility_pins: preserve relevant messages, scorecards, schedules, and witness notes
scenarios.task: Review this workplace complaint as a neutral employee-side preparation memo. Build a chronology, separate direct observations from inference, identify the strongest and weakest retaliation or discrimination indicators, list documents and witnesses to preserve, and propose focused questions for HR or counsel. Do not decide whether a law was violated.
expected_findings: The chronology should compare pre-leave performance, return from leave, promotion denial, complaint, schedule change, exclusion, and warning.
The manager's comment about commitment after parental leave is direct evidence that needs exact context and witnesses.
The close timing between the complaint and adverse schedule or discipline changes supports a retaliation inference but is not conclusive.
The memo should request scorecards, promotion criteria, comparator records, Slack messages, schedules, warning drafts, and witness accounts.
The complaint needs clearer comparator details, who made each decision, and whether performance reasons were documented before the leave.
scenarios.boundary_note: The chronology and evidence categories matter, while the complainant's identity and employer name can be hidden.

scenarios.document:
CONFIDENTIAL WORKPLACE COMPLAINT DRAFT

Complainant: Jordan Okafor (J. Okafor)
Contact: jordan.okafor@private.example, +1 312-555-0162
Internal reference: HR-CHI-2026-044
Employer: Northline Parcel Cooperative

I am a route-analytics lead in the Chicago operation. Before taking parental leave in November 2025, my two most recent performance reviews were rated exceeds expectations, and my manager asked me to lead the spring routing redesign. I returned from parental leave on 3 February 2026.

On 12 February, my manager said during a planning meeting that the promotion panel needed someone whose commitment would not be divided by a new baby. Two coworkers, Lena Ortiz and Michael Chen, were present. On 20 February I learned that the senior operations role went to a colleague with eight months less tenure. HR told me only that the panel chose the candidate with greater schedule flexibility. I have not seen the scorecards or written criteria for the promotion decision.

I reported the comment to an HR partner on 2 March and asked that it be documented. On 9 March my schedule changed from daytime analytical work to a rotating evening dispatch assignment. My manager said everyone needed operational exposure, but no other analytics lead changed shifts. On 18 March I was removed from the routing redesign Slack channel.

On 27 March I received my first written warning for a forecast delivered four hours late. I had sent a message the prior day explaining that the source data had not arrived. A draft of the warning appears to have been created before the missed-data message, but I have only a screenshot showing the file timestamp.

I believe the promotion denial and later changes relate to parental leave and my HR report. I did not hear every conversation and cannot say who directed the schedule change. The review should preserve relevant messages, scorecards, schedules, and witness notes, and distinguish facts I observed from my inferences.
